threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You start calling the Overground the 'Orange Line' without knowing it’s actually a train, not a Tube.
Caught a night bus last week and saw a guy playing an accordion while a couple argued over whose turn it was to pay for takeout. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really living in Neukölln when I saw a street performer juggling flaming torches while a group of kids on scooters cheered him on.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find techno parties in abandoned warehouses alongside sausage stands selling currywurst at 4 AM. It's a wild mix of old and new.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name all the taco spots that still have their old-school menus, not just the trendy ones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo waiting for the 6 at 3 AM. He got on, looked around, and said, 'Well, at least someone's dressed for the occasion.'

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the nightlife, but the real charm is in the quiet morning chatter at the bakery on Carrer Verdi.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to sit on the benches in Plaça del Sol. They haven’t yet embraced the art of people-watching.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'no. 30 bus' is just a quirky route instead of a lifeline that takes you everywhere worth going.
Caught a late 59 last night, only seven of us on board. The driver sang 'Wonderwall' at every stop. It was bizarrely comforting.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? Hearing a grandma yell at her cat from her balcony while a group of kids blasted techno below.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a café that doubles as a punk record shop—coffee and vinyl coexisting amid the chaos of creative energy.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: If they don't flinch when a dog blocks the Muni tracks, they're a local. Tourists panic like the world’s ending. True San Franciscan move.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus that stopped because a guy decided to have a loud karaoke session. Muni's never dull, that's for sure. Just another day in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just hop on any tram, but they often miss the secret stops where the locals actually get off. Like, all the best bars are just a 5-minute walk from those tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They'll be the ones taking selfies with the Gaudí buildings, oblivious to the street performers just a few steps away.
